routes.label: Separate cases by the parents' stores

question: Rabbits Peter and Pauline have three offspring—Flopsie, Mopsie, and Cottontail. These five rabbits are to be distributed to four different pet stores so that no store gets both a parent and a child. It is not required that every store gets a rabbit. In how many different ways can this be done?
solution:
Placing the parents first tells us exactly which stores are forbidden to the children. The parents either share a store or occupy different stores.

If Peter and Pauline share a store, choose that store in \(4\) ways. Each of the three distinct children can then independently go to any of the other \(3\) stores. This gives
\[
4\cdot3^3=108
\]
assignments.

If the parents occupy different stores, Peter has \(4\) choices and Pauline has \(3\) remaining choices. Each child can independently go to either of the \(2\) stores containing no parent. This gives
\[
4\cdot3\cdot2^3=96
\]
assignments.

These two cases are disjoint and include every possible placement of the parents. Within each case, specifying the store of each named rabbit determines exactly one distribution. Children may share stores, and empty stores are allowed, so no further restrictions are needed. The total is
\[
108+96=\boxed{204},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
